rules.explanation: Complaint: not cooling — defrost failure is a common cause.
Complaint: not cooling — sealed system must be considered.
Complaint: weak fresh food cooling — airflow / damper issues common.
Complaint: weak FF cooling — defrost failure can leave FZ cold and FF warm.
Complaint: weak FF cooling — check FF door gasket and alignment.
Complaint: weak freezer cooling — sealed system is a primary suspect.
Complaint: weak FZ cooling — iced evaporator from defrost failure is common.
Complaint: weak FZ cooling — condenser fan and coil cleanliness affect freezer first.
Complaint: weak cooling — temperature checks will split airflow vs sealed system.
Complaint: weak cooling — sealed system remains on the differential.
Complaint: frost / ice buildup points to defrost system.
Complaint: ice maker issue.
Complaint: water dispenser issue.
Complaint: noisy / vibrating — condenser and evaporator fans are primary suspects.
Complaint: noisy / vibrating — compressor hum or refrigerant flow still possible.
Noise at rear / bottom — condenser fan and compressor share this zone.
Noise localized to rear / bottom — condenser fan blade or bearing is a primary suspect.
Noise at rear / bottom — compressor mount hum or refrigerant flow alongside condenser fan.
Noise inside fresh food — evaporator fan or damper airflow is the likely source.
Noise inside freezer — evaporator fan, ice drag, or defrost path favored over rear condenser fan.
Noise at dispenser / ice area — ice maker auger, valve, or fill path.
Noise hard to localize — keep both fan zones and sealed system in play.
Poor condenser coil or fan area condition — heat rejection and airflow compromised.
Condenser area in poor condition — check fan blade, motor, and coil cleanliness.
Condenser area fair — coil cleaning or minor fan issue possible.
Fresh food compartment above normal range.
Fresh food temperature normal — air leak less likely.
Freezer compartment not cold enough.
Freezer cold but fresh food warm — classic defrost/airflow pattern.
Heavy frost observed — defrost system failure likely.
Poor evaporator frost pattern — possible defrost or airflow issue.
Door alignment good — air leak less likely.
Door alignment bad — air leak likely.
Gasket in poor condition — warm air infiltration likely.
Gasket good — air leak less likely.
Door alignment good — ruled out as air leak cause.
Door alignment bad — confirmed air leak path.
Gasket in poor condition — confirmed air leak path.
Gasket good — ruled out as air leak cause.
Compressor not running — sealed system or electrical issue.
Compressor not running when called for.
Compressor running — start device likely OK.
Evaporator fan not running — airflow failure.
Evaporator fan confirmed not running.
Condenser fan not running — heat rejection compromised.
Condenser fan confirmed not running.
Defrost heater open (OL) — heater failure confirmed.
Open defrost heater strongly supports defrost system failure.
Defrost heater resistance normal — heater unlikely failed.
Heater ohms normal — full defrost failure less likely (check thermostat/board).
Open defrost terminator — heater circuit cannot complete.
Defrost thermostat open at frosted evaporator — terminator failed.
Blown defrost thermal fuse — no defrost heat possible.
Defrost/cabinet thermistor reading out of range.
Thermistor open or shorted — sensor failure likely.
Compressor run amps out of range.
Supply voltage out of range — check electrical supply and board.
Freezer holding temperature while fresh food is warm, with a failed damper/air tower — airflow routing issue, not sealed system.
Split-temp pattern with evaporator fan confirmed off — iced tower or fan motor likely.
Customer reported weak FF cooling; measured split confirms airflow/defrost over sealed system.
Whole-box failure with both compartments out of range — prioritize sealed system and compressor path.
Compressor runs but cannot pull load — sealed system restriction/leak or weak compressor.
Frost buildup with fan not running — evaporator fan failure or iced fan blade.
Visual frost with defrost heater open at meter — heater is root cause.
Warm freezer with condenser fan off — poor heat rejection / high head pressure.
FF warming with bad gasket — section air leak before chasing damper or defrost.
No/slow water with critically warm FF — frozen reservoir or fill tube common on side-by-sides.
No ice with warm fresh food — ice maker often secondary to FF cooling failure.
Compressor off with bad supply voltage — check electrical supply before sealed system.
FZ cold, FF warm, with clogged evaporator frost pattern — defrost/airflow failure.
Dead warm box with compressor off — start relay, overload, or control.
Noisy complaint with poor condenser condition — fan motor, blade, or restricted coil likely.
Noisy with bad condenser area — suspect condenser fan motor, bearing, or blade contact.
Condenser fan runs but area is bad — bearing noise, blade rub, or dirty coil under load.
Noisy with compressor running — isolate fan vs compressor mount or refrigerant noise.
Noisy with evap fan off — stalled or seized evap motor can chatter before stopping.
Condenser fan motor amps out of range — motor or bearing path supported.
Condenser fan amp draw abnormal — airflow / heat rejection compromised.
Noisy complaint with abnormal condenser fan amps — motor or bearing failure likely.
Normal fan amps with bad condenser area — coil restriction or cleaning before motor replace.
Compressor running with noisy complaint and bad condenser — favors airflow/fan over compressor start.
Noisy with bad condenser fan operation — blade, bearing, or restricted airflow despite motor spin.
Damaged condenser fan blade or housing with noise complaint — replace fan even if motor runs.
Fan motor runs but blade or housing is bad — classic noisy condenser fan path.
Noisy with bad evaporator fan condition — ice drag, loose blade, or motor bearing.
Condenser fan runs but blade, bearing, or airflow is bad.
Samsung 22E/22C — freezer or fridge evaporator fan fault (F-FAN / C-FAN).
Samsung 5E/SE — defrost thermistor (F-DEF-Sensor) out of range.
Samsung 84C — compressor lock / startup failure; check inverter and sealed system.
Samsung 86E — inverter compressor fault; inverter PCB or harness.
Samsung O FF / Cooling Off — demo mode; compressor disabled intentionally.
Samsung RD — fresh-food damper motor/heater fault; weak FF cooling common.
Complaint: error code on display — verify code meaning before sealed-system work.
Cooling Off / demo — compressor disabled intentionally; exit mode before parts.
Dead or partial display — hinge LVDS, panel PCB, or main board comm.
Door alarm — door ajar, gasket interference, or failed reed switch.
Samsung 8E — fridge compartment (R-Sensor) thermistor fault.
Samsung 14E — humidity sensor out of range at CN40.
Samsung 33E — ice pipe heater open at CN90.
Samsung 40E/40C — ice maker compartment fan fault.
Samsung 41E/41Er — main ↔ display panel communication.
Samsung 44E/44Er — main ↔ inverter communication at CN70.
Samsung 46E/46Er — main ↔ I/O expander communication.
Samsung 47E/47Er — dispenser panel communication.
Samsung 52E/52Er — WiFi module comm; cooling usually unaffected.
Samsung 21E — top-hinge LVDS harness; often pairs with PC ER.
Samsung PC ER — door hinge / LVDS communication fault.
Samsung OF OF — Cooling Off / exhibition mode.
Fans run with compressor off — classic Cooling Off / demo before sealed-system diagnosis.
Demo mode ruled out — proceed with sealed system / defrost differential.
Door reed switch not toggling — fan interlock, lamp, and alarm faults.
Weak FF only with bad damper — RD / air tower path.
Panel unresponsive — UI PCB, hinge harness, or main board comm.
Thermistor voltage out of range at board connector — sensor or harness.
Evap fan feedback below 7 V — F-FAN/C-FAN path per Samsung §4-2.
Inverter IPM supply under 13.5 V — comp start failure / 84C / 86E path.
Samsung defrost heater out of 63 Ω ±7% spec — open or shorted.
Cold freezer + warm FF + bad damper — classic RD / air tower pattern.
86E with low IPM voltage — inverter board or harness before compressor.
LG F dH — freezer defrost heater failed to complete cycle; Test Mode 3 voltage/Ω.
LG r dH — fresh-food defrost heater path; CON9 103–119 Ω.
LG F dS — freezer defrost thermistor CON4 pins 22–21 out of range.
LG E FF — freezer evaporator fan; ice blockage or motor/PCB output.
LG E rF — refrigerator compartment fan; weak FF cooling common.
LG E IF / ER — icing compartment fan fault (Craft Ice room).
LG E CF — condenser fan motor; grille blockage or PCB output.
LG E CO — main ↔ display communication; hinge CON101 harness.
LG E CH — high-side refrigerant leak cycle; sealed-system repair.
LG E CL — low-side leak cycle on R-600a linear compressor system.
LG E FS — freezer cabinet thermistor CON4 pins 18–17.
LG E rS — fresh-food thermistor out of range.
LG E IS — icing room / Craft Ice compartment sensor.
LG E CS — Full Convert / pantry drawer thermistor.
LG E Od — ThinQ WiFi modem comm; cooling usually unaffected.
LG E ID — ice maker tray thermistor fault.
LG E IU — ice maker kit motor/heater/hall electrical fault.
LG display/demo mode — OFF on panel, all cooling disabled §13-1-15.
LG fan supply below 11.4 V in Test Mode 1 — motor or main PCB output.
No 112–116 V at heater in Test Mode 3 — PCB relay or Fuse-M.
LG F defrost heater out of 62–70 Ω — open element or blown Fuse-M.
E FF with low fan voltage — F-fan motor or CON3 harness before PCB.
F dH with open F heater — replace heater/Fuse-M before main PCB.
Condenser still suspect if coils were not verified clean on not-cooling call.
Insignia/Midea E2 — freezer compartment temp sensor.
Insignia/Midea E6 — display ↔ main CN9 communication.
E9 high temp alarm — check door gasket and airflow before sealed system.
Frigidaire Er t1 — freezer temp sensor open/short.
Frigidaire demo/showroom mode — compressor may be off.
Whirlpool ice maker E4 dry cycle — no water detected at mold.
WRT defrost heater out of ~30 Ω installed spec — open or shorted.
Defrost bimetal open at frosted evaporator — heater circuit cannot complete.
PTC start device open or out of cold ~5 Ω spec — compressor won't start.
Ice maker harness thermal fuse open — replace harness; check mold heater.
Whirlpool RD — defrost heater fault; WRT ~30 Ω at heater terminals.
Whirlpool DF — defrost failure; check heater, bimetal, timer/ADC.
PTC start device — cold ~5 Ω; allow 10 min cool-down between start attempts.
Ice maker thermal fuse open — dead ice maker until harness replaced.
Temperature control at OFF — unit will not cool until control is advanced.
Heavy frost + open WRT defrost heater — primary defrost path.
WRT311 defrost heater out of 30–42 Ω (W10674984) — open or wrong heater.
ADC test mode entered but no 120 V at P2–P6 — ADC relay or harness.
Not cooling + no ADC P6–P4 output — thermostat, ADC, or wiring before sealed system.
IM E2 — motor home not found; L–M should read 8800 Ω off support.
IM E3 — mold heater timeout; L–H should read 72 Ω.
Modular ice maker L–H heater out of 72 Ω spec — open mold heater.
Modular ice maker L–M motor open — 8800 Ω expected off support.
Ice maker harness thermal fuse open — replace harness; check L–H heater.
Dry cycle — no water at mold; check N–V valve voltage and fill.
WRT311 ADC 2000 defrost test — thermostat OFF/ON sequence; verify P2–P6 heater voltage.
